title: Morning Headlines
intro: A landmark US-Iran ceasefire agreement reshapes the Middle East while NATO faces a fundamental rethink, the Fed spooks markets, and Washington escalates its denaturalization drive.

items.title: US and Iran Sign 14-Point Ceasefire Memorandum of Understanding
items.subtitle: CNBC / NBC News / CNN / CBS News / NPR
items.summary: President Trump and Iranian President Pezeshkian remotely signed a 14-point MOU on June 17 — brokered by Pakistan at the G7 — halting all military operations, reopening the Strait of Hormuz, lifting the US naval blockade of Iranian ports, and launching a 60-day window to negotiate a final nuclear deal under IAEA supervision. The agreement marks the most significant US-Iran diplomatic breakthrough since the 2015 JCPOA and ends a war that had roiled global energy markets.

items.title: Hegseth Announces 'NATO 3.0' and Six-Month Review of US Forces in Europe
items.subtitle: NPR / CBS News / The Washington Post / NBC News
items.summary: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth traveled to Brussels on June 18 to announce a Pentagon review of American troop and asset commitments in Europe and unveiled a concept he called 'NATO 3.0' — pushing European allies to take primary responsibility for their own conventional defense as the US draws down. He also publicly blasted allies for refusing to grant US forces basing rights during the Iran war, calling the refusal 'shameful.'

items.title: Fed Chair Warsh's Hawkish Dot Plot Sparks Sharp Market Selloff
items.subtitle: TheStreet / Charles Schwab / InvestingCube
items.summary: The Federal Reserve held rates at 3.50–3.75% on June 17 but Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's first press conference shocked markets: nine of eighteen officials projected a rate hike before year-end, removing prior language about further 'adjustments,' and Warsh repeatedly stressed 'price stability' with inflation still running at 4.2% YoY. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq plunged on the news before staging a partial recovery Thursday; US markets are closed Friday for Juneteenth.

items.title: DOJ Plans to Revoke Citizenship of More Than 250 Naturalized Americans by October
items.subtitle: CNN / CBS News / NPR / The Hill
items.summary: The Trump administration is planning to file at least 250 denaturalization cases against foreign-born naturalized citizens by fall, according to a Justice Department official — an unprecedented escalation compared with fewer than 10 cases per year historically. The DOJ has already filed 29 cases in under two months, and legal experts warn the push extends well beyond the fraud cases historically targeted to include a broader category of naturalized citizens.

items.title: Obama Presidential Center and Library Opens to the Public on Juneteenth
items.subtitle: CBS News / ABC7 Chicago / The Obama Foundation
items.summary: After more than a decade in planning and years of legal and community battles over its location, the Obama Presidential Center in Chicago's Jackson Park opened to the public on June 19 — deliberately timed to coincide with the Juneteenth federal holiday. The campus includes a museum, public gardens, an athletic center, and a Chicago Public Library branch, with most of the grounds free and open without tickets.
